su15.finding: Candidate solved L1-L3 in14/17/21 actions versus15/23/69 baseline, then stalled on L5(two invaders), spending103actions there. It repeatedly planned greedy kiting/assembly with inaccurate invader forecasts. The observed loss is not evidence of forgetting the earlier basics.

specific_program_error.description: guarded() only raises on no p/Y and a fixed tag whitelist. Subsequent actual calls use labelsD1/W1/W3/etc outside that whitelist. It therefore printsok after material destruction; even wholesale p-to-M conversion can pass. Its computed total is never used to enforce an invariant.
specific_program_error.limitation: Observed source and stdout establish a guard failure, not that correcting the guard alone would win.

su15.wrong_memory_causality: Not established. The L4 rule describes nearest-piece chase/UNDO/fastdelivery, which is not a full model of L5 double-invader dynamics; candidate revises speed/dash assumptions from new observations rather than simply copying a stored failed action tail.

overall_conclusion: Both regressions are real observed outcomes, but no specific wrong-memory-rule-to-bad-action causal chain was established. sc25 has substantial first-level loss before any solvedmemory exists. su15 reaches L5 quickly, then fails to build/execute a correct model of the two-invader problem and has a concrete ineffective execution guard. Do not erase these losses or attribute all of them to memory.
next_research_implication: Preserve frozen032 and await actual formal score. Current-level world-model/search and verification of generated code remain a specific research opportunity; this audit does not demonstrate that any proposed fix improves score and does not justify reopening030 unchanged.
